reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Reviewed the resource-level context, full EnrollmentRequest StructureDefinition report, deterministic aggregate, and the supplied resource-review/rubric/fresh-review guidance. The behavior findings in scope were only shared Resource/DomainResource context; because EnrollmentRequest is not itself Resource or DomainResource, those findings were considered as background rather than scored as EnrollmentRequest-specific behavior breaks. The deterministic aggregate was compared only after forming the resource-level judgment.

r4Maturity.effectMd: The R4 baseline is trial-use/FMM 0, which creates weak stability pressure. Enrollment workflows can still have payer and business impact, but this low maturity means a reverse-direction, additive target widening should not be escalated as a standards-level R4-to-R6 break without stronger evidence of production reliance or avoidable design churn.

overall.oneLineConclusion: EnrollmentRequest has a stable R4-to-R6 content model; the only local material change is allowing Group as an additional candidate target, which is mainly an R6-to-R4/mixed-version policy issue.

reasoning.thesisMd: EnrollmentRequest keeps the same resource identity and almost the same local content model. The local element set, element names, cardinalities, local type codes, modifier/summary flags, constraints, and observed `fm-status` code set are stable. Existing R4 instances with no candidate or a Patient candidate remain acceptable under the R6 local definition. Therefore a resource-level R4-to-R6 migration program is not already unavoidable.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: The actual migration shape is low material change. There is no resource removal, rename, split, merge, local element removal, mandatory addition, target narrowing, required-code rejection, or new local invariant. The sole local finding widens `EnrollmentRequest.candidate` from `Reference(Patient)` to `Reference(Patient | Group)` while preserving the same path and 0..1 cardinality.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: Because there is no unavoidable resource-level migration program and no direct R4-to-R6 local break, there is no special resource-level break-avoidance posture to apply for EnrollmentRequest. This does not mean future breaks would be free; it means the current reviewed delta does not contain an avoidable local break whose preservation would materially change R4-to-R6 migration cost.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: The Group target addition does require policy for R6 data sent to R4 systems, but it is not an old-valid/new-invalid break. Keeping the base target Patient-only or forcing Group enrollment through extensions would reduce downgrade friction while failing the apparent R6 goal of first-class group enrollment. A separate group-candidate element would add duplicate subject representations and would not be easier for R4 receivers. The remaining work is local downgrade/business policy, not a low-cost base compatibility preservation opportunity.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: No direct OperationDefinition, SearchParameter, or HTTP behavior finding was assigned to EnrollmentRequest. The shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings include real generic API and search compatibility issues, but under the review rules they remain context only for this resource and should be resolved in the base Resource/DomainResource or behavior reviews rather than driving an EnrollmentRequest-specific migration conclusion.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: I agree with the deterministic aggregate's `No` major-migration conclusion, `low-material-change` migration shape, and `no-special-break-avoidance-needed` compatibility posture. The important nuance is that the high-impact structure finding is not meaningless: `candidate=Group` can be business-significant in R6-to-R4 exchange. It just does not make R4-to-R6 EnrollmentRequest migration broadly unavoidable or identify an avoidable base-design break.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: The official narrative diff, ballot rationale, production prevalence, and deployment profiles were not available. Those could affect migration guidance for group enrollment workflows, but the computable local delta is small and high-confidence enough to support the resource-level conclusion.

findingConsiderations.title: EnrollmentRequest.candidate now permits Group as well as Patient
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the only local material finding and it demonstrates the resource's actual migration shape. It is a target widening at the same 0..1 path, so R4 Patient candidates remain valid in R6 and no broad forward migration program is triggered. It still matters operationally for R6-to-R4 exchange because a Group candidate cannot be losslessly reduced to a single Patient without business policy.

findingConsiderations.title: Resource $meta-add is removed from R6 core
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is a high-impact generic Resource operation issue, but it is present in the context as shared Resource behavior rather than a direct EnrollmentRequest behavior finding. It should not be multiplied into a resource-specific conclusion for EnrollmentRequest.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 invocation matrix changes instance-level Resource $validate request semantics
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The `$validate` invocation change can affect validation clients for any resource, including EnrollmentRequest instances, but the finding is generic Resource behavior. It is important background for platform migration plans, not evidence that EnrollmentRequest's own StructureDefinition has a major migration burden.

findingConsiderations.title: Core special/profile search parameters changed type metadata for _content, _text, _query, and _profile
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The shared search-parameter metadata change is relevant to generic search tooling, but it is not a direct EnrollmentRequest search finding and does not alter the resource-level assessment of the local EnrollmentRequest model.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: For mixed R4/R6 exchange, document an explicit policy for R6 `EnrollmentRequest.candidate` references to `Group`: reject/quarantine, carry via a profiled extension, or split into patient-specific requests only when business rules make that semantically correct. Do not silently coerce a Group candidate to one Patient.

Keep EnrollmentRequest standards-review attention low unless new implementation evidence appears; migration notes and tests should cover absent candidate, Patient candidate, and Group candidate cases.
Track the shared Resource/DomainResource operation and search behavior findings in the generic behavior/base-resource review stream rather than treating them as EnrollmentRequest-specific breaks.

caveats: No official R4-to-R6 EnrollmentRequest change narrative or ballot rationale was available in the local inputs.
Implementation-guide profiles and payer-specific production contracts may impose stricter candidate rules than the base core resource.
Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were considered as context only, per the review rules.
